page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-120g-32vram is a dedicated metal GPU server designed for accelerated multimedia processing, virtual desktop infrastructure, and concurrent inference tasks. The instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs derived from 6 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning stands at 120 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 10 GB per virtual core. Storage is provided via a bundled 700 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by one included public IPv4 address.

Accelerated compute is driven by two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM, with 16 GB assigned per GPU. The underlying Intel Xeon host processor supports standard enterprise instruction sets, including AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI), AES-NI, and BMI2. In synthetic CPU benchmarks, the system consistently achieves mid-tier scores, recording 1,703.68 in stress-ng single-core, 21,197.07 in stress-ng multi-core, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,742.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 120.27 GB/sec, while write operations reach 67.84 GB/sec.

Performance benchmarks show balanced handling across moderate data-processing pipelines, demonstrated by 22.01 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.08 GB/sec in static web throughput. For artificial intelligence tasks, the dual-GPU architecture demonstrates capable prompt processing for smaller models, achieving 1,011.54 tokens per second on a 135M parameter LLM. However, scaling to larger architectures exposes throughput limitations; prompt processing for 7B parameter models drops to 22.81 tokens per second, placing it in the lower quartile of GPU benchmarks.

This configuration delivers solid resource density for streaming, remote graphics, and multi-user environments rather than massive transformer training. The dedicated hardware design eliminates multi-tenant noisy-neighbor interference while offering substantial memory and local NVMe storage. It is best suited for video transcoding, high-density VDI deployments, lightweight AI model serving, and parallel microservices requiring dedicated GPU acceleration.

Accelerated compute is handled by two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs providing a combined 32 GB of VRAM. With a memory-to-core allocation of 10 GB per vCPU, the system maintains stable mid-range performance across synthetic benchmarks, including 21,197.07 in stress-ng multi-core and 9,742.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Network and I/O pipelines demonstrate high transactional throughput, recording 22.01 million Redis SET operations per second. Machine learning benchmarks show strong execution on smaller models, though prompt evaluation slows down considerably on 7B architectures. This instance provides a cost-effective, high-density platform for concurrent video streaming, virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), Android cloud emulation, and lightweight deep learning inference.
